issue: ts-no-typecheck claims 'no CI step runs tsc --noEmit -p <suite>' (docstring :22, finding text :206, e2e-tester.md:115) but passes on ANY tsc line anywhere: an app-level root package.json script `tsc --noEmit -p app/javascript`, or a qa/package.json `typecheck` script that no CI surface ever invokes. The scaffold setup-qa.md:186 creates exactly that script, so a fresh scaffold passes the gate with CI never type-checking the suite -- the 'strict is enforced by nothing' state this PR exists to catch.
repro: qa/e2e/{tsconfig.json strict, a.spec.ts}, root package.json {scripts:{types:'tsc --noEmit -p app/javascript'}}, no CI -> run() == ([], 1). Same with only qa/package.json {scripts:{typecheck:'tsc --noEmit -p e2e/tsconfig.json'}}.
fix_options: Require the step to target the suite: -p/--project resolving under qa/ (or --prefix qa / cd qa context), and count a package.json script only when a CI surface runs it (npm|yarn|pnpm [--prefix qa] run <name>).
Add negative fixtures: app-only tsc, defined-but-uninvoked script; mutation for each.

issue: ANY matches only `: any`, `as any`, exact `<any>`, `any[]`, `Array<any>`. Explicit any in `Record<string, any>`, `Map<any, string>`, `type T = any`, `<T = any>`, `string | any`, `keyof any` is not flagged. e2e-tester.md:115 tells agents the gate 'refuses ... an undeclared explicit any'; Record<string, any> is among the most common forms in Playwright fixtures.
repro: explicit_anys('f.ts','const h: Record<string, any> = {};\n') == [] (also Map<any,string>, type T = any, <T = any>, string | any).
fix_options: After _blank, match the keyword itself: (?<![\w$.])any(?![\w$]) excluding an object-key position (any\s*:) -- covers every type position; add fixtures for each form above plus `{ any: 1 }` and `obj.any` as negatives.
Or narrow the doctrine sentence to the listed forms (weaker: the owner's rule is 'no any type').

issue: _load_json strips /*...*/ with a regex that ignores strings, and strips // only at line start. A correct strict tsconfig with a paths alias (`"@fixtures/*": ["./fixtures/*"]` followed later by a `**/*.ts` include) or a trailing `// comment` fails json.loads and is reported ts-not-strict 'unreadable tsconfig' -- a red gate on a valid, common config.
repro: tsconfig {compilerOptions:{baseUrl:'.', paths:{'@fixtures/*':['./fixtures/*']}, strict:true}, include:['e2e/**/*.ts']} -> JSONDecodeError; '{"compilerOptions":{"strict":true // yes\n}}' -> JSONDecodeError.
fix_options: Strip JSONC with a string-aware character scanner (the file already has one in _blank; factor a variant that keeps string contents).
Add both repros as CONTROL fixtures that must read strict.

issue: Doctrine prescribes `npx tsc --noEmit -p qa/e2e/tsconfig.json` from the repo root, but setup-qa.md:182 installs typescript in qa/package.json, and the gate's own fixture (check_ts_strict.py:216) and the downstream step use `npx --prefix qa tsc`. From root, npx will not find qa/node_modules/.bin/tsc [Recall: npx then resolves the unrelated `tsc` npm package].
fix_options: Prescribe `npm --prefix qa run typecheck` (the scaffolded script) or `npx --prefix qa tsc --noEmit -p qa/e2e/tsconfig.json`.

issue: Only **/*.ts is scanned and counted for applicability; .tsx (Playwright component tests), .mts, .cts are neither scanned for any nor make the check applicable (a qa/ with only .mts exits 3).
fix_options: Glob *.ts, *.tsx, *.mts, *.cts.

issue: `"strict": true, "noImplicitAny": false` (or any strict-family flag set false) reads as strict; the gate's claim is that the suite is strict.
fix_options: Treat an explicit false on a strict-family member (noImplicitAny, strictNullChecks, ...) as ts-not-strict; fixture.

issue: A non-relative extends (`@tsconfig/strictest/tsconfig.json`) or a TS 5 array extends (`["./base.json"]`) returns False -> ts-not-strict on a suite that is strict. Docstring says only 'relative extends' but the finding text says strict 'is not true', not 'could not be followed'.
fix_options: Follow array extends; resolve package extends via qa/node_modules, or report 'could not follow extends' distinctly.

issue: Docstring says rules apply to 'the tsconfig nearest its .ts files'; run() checks every qa/**/tsconfig*.json and never walks up (a suite using the repo-root tsconfig is reported 'no tsconfig').
fix_options: Reword the docstring to what run() does, or implement nearest-ancestor resolution.

issue: KNOWN LIMITS names only a `//` in a regex literal; a quote in one (`const re = /'/; f(x as any);`) opens a string to end of line and hides a real any on that line (false negative).
fix_options: Extend the KNOWN LIMITS sentence to quotes in regex literals, or add a minimal regex-literal heuristic.

issue: PR body says 'Fixes #1447' into dev; CLAUDE.md checklist step 9 and Git flow say Refs, never a closing keyword, on dev. The owner's 2026-09-29 decision (close on dev merge) appears to supersede CLAUDE.md, and recent dev PRs are mixed -- CLAUDE.md is stale, not necessarily this PR. Human call.
fix_options: Update CLAUDE.md Git flow to the owner's decision, or switch this PR to Refs.

issue: ts-no-typecheck still passes a step that enforces nothing. Each of these CI files returns [] (no finding): `run: npx tsc --noEmit -p qa/e2e/tsconfig.json || true`; `... || echo skipped`; `...; exit 0`; `npm --prefix qa run typecheck || true`; a step with `continue-on-error: true`; a step with `if: false`; `run: echo ok # npx tsc -p qa/e2e/tsconfig.json` (trailing comment); `run: echo npx tsc -p qa/...`. TSC (:69) and RUNNER (:71) stop at `|`/`;` so the `|| true` is never seen, and the scan is per line (:293) so step keys are never read. The docstring (:27) says the rule finds a line that type-checks the suite, and e2e-tester.md:110 says strict is enforced by nothing without that step. A swallowed verdict is the class CLAUDE.md names; `|| true` and `continue-on-error` are what a team adds while it fixes type errors.
fix_options: Parse per STEP (buffer lines to the next `- `), skip a step whose `continue-on-error` is true or whose `if:` is `false`/`${{ false }}`; drop unquoted text after ` #`; refuse a tsc/runner segment followed by `||` or a later `exit 0`/`true` segment, or preceded by echo/printf. Add a selftest fixture and a mutation for each.

issue: The docstring (:29) says -p resolves from the step's `working-directory:`, but only when that key comes BEFORE `run:`. `- run: npx tsc --noEmit -p e2e/tsconfig.json` followed by `  working-directory: qa` (valid, common YAML order) gives a false ts-no-typecheck on a CI that does type-check the suite. The gate goes red on a correct project.
fix_options: Same fix as B1: collect the whole step first, then resolve working-directory, then evaluate its run lines. Add the run-then-working-directory fixture.

issue: Job-level `defaults: run: working-directory: qa` is ignored: NEW_STEP resets workdir to '.', so `- run: npx tsc -p e2e/tsconfig.json` under those defaults is a false ts-no-typecheck.
fix_options: Track `defaults.run.working-directory` per job as the reset value, or name it in KNOWN LIMITS.

issue: A `run: |` block with `cd qa` on one line and `npx tsc -p e2e/tsconfig.json` on the next is a false ts-no-typecheck: only `cd <dir> &&` on the same line is resolved. The docstring says `cd <dir> &&`, so this is a limit, but it is not listed in KNOWN LIMITS.
fix_options: Carry a bare `cd <dir>` forward to later lines of the same step, or add it to KNOWN LIMITS.

issue: ANY flags `any` where it is not a type: `@any class X {}`, `class X { #any = 1 }`, `const { any } = o;`, `let any = 1;` (each gives 1 finding). Rare, but each forces an allow-any declaration with no real `any` behind it.
fix_options: Add `#@` to the lookbehind; name shorthand destructuring and an identifier called any in KNOWN LIMITS.

issue: `const v = ok ? x as any : y;` gives 0 findings. The object-key lookahead `(?!\s*\??\s*:)` reads any `any :` as a key. KNOWN LIMITS (:47) lists only the conditional type `? any : never`, not a cast inside a ternary.
fix_options: Treat `any` as a key only when the previous significant character is `{`, `,`, `;`, `(` or a line start. That fixes the ternary cast and the conditional type. Otherwise list the ternary cast in KNOWN LIMITS.

issue: ALLOW is matched on the RAW line, so a marker inside a string is honoured: `const s = "// ts-strict: allow-any -- x"; f(x as any);` gives 0 findings. No negative fixture for this.
fix_options: Accept the marker only inside a comment span (the raw text at a position the blanker removed after `//` or `/*`); add a fixture.

issue: `const q = i++ / 2; f(x as any); const z = w / 3;` gives 0 findings: `+` is in REGEX_AFTER, so the `/` after a postfix `++` opens a regex that runs to the next `/` and blanks the `as any`. `a / b / c`, `(a) / 2 / (b)` and `arr[0] / 2` are read correctly.
fix_options: Treat `++`/`--` as the end of a value (look at the two previous characters), or add it to KNOWN LIMITS.

issue: A cycle does not hang: a 2-cycle and a self-extend return in 0.0 s. But it is cut off silently at depth 8 and read as strict, though tsc refuses a circular extends. An array extends that lists itself is exponential: 4 self-entries took 5.2 s (4^8 loads), and it grows as k^8.
fix_options: Carry a visited set down the chain and raise Unfollowed('circular extends'); memoise each resolved path.

issue: A tsconfig saved with a UTF-8 BOM (tsc accepts it, and Windows editors write it) raises JSONDecodeError 'Unexpected UTF-8 BOM', which is reported as ts-not-strict 'unreadable tsconfig'.
fix_options: read_text(encoding='utf-8-sig').

issue: The nine strict-family members match the typescriptlang.org/tsconfig#strict list [Recall: TS 5.6+, where strictBuiltinIteratorReturn joined], but neither the CHANGELOG citation nor the STRICT_FAMILY comment (:81) names the TypeScript version. CLAUDE.md's gate asks for the citation AND the version boundary.
fix_options: Add the TypeScript version the list was verified against (5.6+ for strictBuiltinIteratorReturn) to the CHANGELOG entry and the comment at :81.

issue: The CONTROL fixture CI_YML (:350) and the config/ci.rb fixture (:443) use `npx --prefix qa tsc`, the form the CHANGELOG records as INCONCLUSIVE and the doctrine avoids. Nothing is prescribed with it, but the gate's own control example is the unverified form.
fix_options: Make CI_YML use `npm --prefix qa run typecheck` with a qa/package.json in `base`. Keep a direct `npx tsc -p qa/...` fixture for the direct form.
